source.title: Unlearning via RMU is mostly shallow (LessWrong)

page_placements.theme: Internal analyses: changes concentrated late or along a direction, target representations stay close to the original

record.file_problem: none; full informal research post and comments are present
record.tranche_reason: The post tests directional ablation on an RMU-unlearned model and finds substantial but incomplete recovery, refining the broad claim that RMU's effect is mainly shallow.
record.gate_note: The post reports WMDP performance-gap recovery after ablating two dataset-specific directions simultaneously. It also describes restored activation similarity and norms, but those measures do not themselves show recovery of knowledge. Qualitative prompt examples illustrate coherence; they are not scored as knowledge-recovery results. Mentioned fine-tuning recovery in a comment is attributed to another researcher and is not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The post applies an inference-time directional ablation to the released Zephyr_RMU model. It scores WMDP-Bio and WMDP-Cyber recovery as a share of the RMU-to-baseline gap. The result bears directly on version C (recovery by internal edits) and on A's assertion that simple attacks do not recover the knowledge. The finding is that recovery is substantial but incomplete, which argues for restating 'RMU is shallow' as 'partly shallow'.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that RMU works partly by flooding the residual stream with junk, which is a shallow effect that directional ablation largely undoes. They also conclude it partly works through a deeper mechanism that leaves knowledge inaccessible even after ablation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an already RMU-fine-tuned Zephyr model and tests a directional-ablation intervention; it does not reproduce RMU training. The extracted directions are dataset-specific difference-in-means directions, and both are ablated together.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery differs by benchmark: ~71% of the Bio performance gap versus ~45% of the Cyber gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablation restores most activation cosine similarity to baseline and baseline-like activation norms from layer 8 on.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RMU's forget-set effect is largely mediated by injecting a large fixed direction into the residual stream at the target layer, which ablation removes.

record.problems: One model pair is studied. The post gives percentage-of-gap recovery rather than the underlying benchmark scores or uncertainty estimates. The hypothesized deeper mechanism is not directly established; the authors say preliminary experiments were inconclusive.
record.rows_left_out: No separately scored rows for the qualitative prompt examples: the post reports coherence and example answers but does not score their knowledge accuracy. The activation-geometry findings are retained as rows r3–r4, but are not linked to a claim version.

untested.parts: Whether RMU brings WMDP accuracy near chance and preserves general ability (MMLU etc.) is not measured. No general-ability score is reported for the ablated model either.
No fine-tuning or relearning experiment. The comment's mention of Fabien Roger's fine-tuning recovery is not this study's result.

Only one model pair (Zephyr-7B RMU) and one unlearning method. Only difference-in-means directions for Bio and Cyber, ablated jointly. The weight-orthogonalization variant is described but not separately scored. The 'deep mechanism' hypothesis was inconclusive.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context attacks.
No robust counter-method tested. Tamper-resistant safeguards are only mentioned in a comment.

missing.what: Absolute WMDP-Bio and WMDP-Cyber accuracies for baseline, RMU and RMU-ablated models, from which the gap percentages are computed. These are needed to judge near-chance status and to compare with other studies.

record.verdict_notes: Informal LessWrong note on a single model pair, with no uncertainty estimates. In a comment, a WMDP author notes that the original paper already acknowledged white-box vulnerability (Figure 14/15). The qualitative ablated answer on the influenza item is coherent but factually wrong, consistent with the incomplete recovery.

versions.untested_parts: Tests whether ablation recovers targeted knowledge after RMU, but does not establish that RMU brought accuracy near chance or preserved general ability.
No fine-tuning or relearning-set recovery experiment.
Tests simultaneous ablation of two dataset-specific directions in one RMU model pair; does not test other directions, models, or unlearning methods.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context-information recovery experiment.

source_check.notes: The post gives recovery only as a share of the gap: no raw accuracies, no uncertainty, no MMLU or other capability check. It also has no control intervention (such as a random direction); the only comparisons are baseline and unablated RMU. The directions need the baseline model's activations, and the author's hypothesis for the deep part is inconclusive.

statements.correction: This post: one difference-in-means 'junk' direction per domain (baseline minus RMU activations, last token of hazardous prompts). The Bio and Cyber directions are projected out together from all intermediate activations of cais/Zephyr_RMU. Recovery: ~71% of the WMDP-Bio gap and ~45% of the WMDP-Cyber gap. The directions use baseline (zephyr-7b-beta) activations.
statements.problem: The ~71% and ~45% figures are right. But the conditions describe the Zephyr-7B-β RMU directions as 'per-layer ground-truth directions'. For this post they are not per-layer: there is one difference-in-means direction per domain, ablated from all layers.

statements.correction: Ablating the junk direction restores most activation similarity with the baseline, and the ablated norms look similar to baseline (figures only, no layer range stated in the text). Baseline and unablated RMU activations diverge, and RMU norms jump, starting at layer 8.
statements.problem: The text says ablation restores most activation similarity and gives baseline-like norms, but this is figure-only. It gives no layer range for the restoration. Layer 8 is where unablated RMU and baseline activations start to diverge and where norms jump.
